newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks maintain momentum in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks maintain momentum in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices maintained momentum in volatile late trade on Friday as investors bounced back from Thursday's electronics freefall to pour more funds into the bellwether sector, brokers said.
Brokers said investment into electronics was not as heavy as in the past four days, calling this a sign that investors were adjusting their strategy and diversifying their holdings.
With 60 minutes left, at 0300 GMT, the benchmark stock index was up 62.6 points or 0.65 percent at 9,634.4, off an intraday high 9,669.74. Turnover was heavy at T$145.3 billion.
"Thursday's electronics freefall has actually helped the market return to its normal condition," said Lin Long-hsien, assistant manager of United Securities.
"It has also brought forth technical rebounds in other sectors which had been neglected in the past few days in the face of red-hot electronics," he said.
The volatile high-tech sector, which had risen six percent on the week before nosediving three percent on Thursday, had rebounded 2.91 percent in late trade on Friday.
Notebook computer maker Inventech was up the seven percent daily limit, rising T$13 to T$207. Computer maker Mitac had also had gained a limit-up T$2.5 to T$39.2.
Automobile shares were enjoying a technical rebound, rising 3.48 percent as a sector to spur the market.
Sanfu Motors was up T$0.75 to T$11.95, while China Motor had risen T$3.5 to T$60.5.
Brokers said with modest rebounds in other industrial sectors, the weighted index should be able to stand above the 9,600 technical resistance level by the close.
